description: The GRAMMAR over conventions — the second-order semiotic operations TV Tropes calls 'Playing With a Trope'. Each is an OPERATION on a convention's EXPECTATION (from narrative_convention), not a flat label: a base expectation is set up, then transformed. This is the Gamma to the tropes' G — the corpus hands the agent both a vocabulary (conventions) and a grammar (these operations). They are the engine of sophistication and of humour (a subversion is the structure of a joke). The agent grounds each from Example-text markers ('Subverted when...', 'Played for laughs'); the transformational if/then content belongs in a trope_play expansion pack as derivation_rules.

concepts.name: played_straight
concepts.definition: The convention is used as-is; the expectation it installs holds and is paid off. The default, against which every other operation is defined.

concepts.name: subverted
concepts.definition: Set up the expectation, then deliberately VIOLATE it. The structural core of surprise and of humour: build a prediction, break it. Distinct from simply not using the convention — the setup must occur for the break to land.

concepts.name: inverted
concepts.definition: Run the convention BACKWARDS — produce its opposite where the convention's outcome was expected. Not a break in the prediction but a reversal of its content.

concepts.name: averted
concepts.definition: The convention is conspicuously NOT used where the frame would lead a viewer to expect it. No setup-and-break; the expectation is simply, pointedly, not honoured. Grounds the convention negatively (its absence is meaningful only because the expectation existed).

concepts.name: lampshaded
concepts.definition: The work SELF-CONSCIOUSLY points out its own use of the convention — meta-awareness, a character or narrator naming the device. Ties to reflective access (Axiom 3): the work models its own structure. Often the seam where humour and intertextuality enter.

concepts.name: deconstructed
concepts.definition: Take the convention SERIOUSLY and follow its real consequences to where they actually lead — usually puncturing the comfortable expectation by honouring it rigorously. The expectation is not broken but pursued past the point the convention normally stops.

concepts.name: reconstructed
concepts.definition: After a deconstruction, rebuild the convention with its problems acknowledged — re-establishing the expectation on new, earned footing.

concepts.name: exaggerated
concepts.definition: Push the convention past its normal intensity until the expectation is overshot. A common humour mechanism (incongruity by degree).

concepts.name: downplayed
concepts.definition: Use the convention in a muted, minimal form — the expectation is gestured at but not fully installed.

concepts.name: zigzagged
concepts.definition: Play, subvert, restore, subvert again — the expectation is repeatedly set up and broken so the viewer can no longer predict which way it will resolve. Higher-order play on the prediction itself.

concepts.name: invoked_defied_exploited
concepts.definition: The CHARACTERS' stance toward the convention as an in-world fact: invoked (a character deliberately causes it), defied (a character refuses to let it happen), exploited (a character uses others' expectation of it). Meaning shifts from author-on-audience to character-on-world; presupposes the convention is itself known.
